Reference implementation (Python 3.12+):
```python
def deduplicate_sorted_in_place(values):
    if not values:
        return 0
    write = 1
    for read in range(1, len(values)):
        if values[read] != values[write - 1]:
            values[write] = values[read]
            write += 1
    return write  # Unique values are now values[:write].

items = [1, 1, 2, 2, 3]
length = deduplicate_sorted_in_place(items)
assert items[:length] == [1, 2, 3]
```
explanation: The read/write pointers retain one copy of each sorted value. Time O(n), auxiliary space O(1); values beyond the returned logical length should be ignored.
